prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single PORTRAIT 9:16 image, 1080x1920 or the highest actually supported native portrait resolution close to 9:16. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 70% of width and central 70% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 13.18. Exact Sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥ १८ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Thus the Field, Knowledge, and the Knowable have been described in brief. My devotee, knowing this through direct realization (vijñāna), attains My very being. Chapter context: Field and knower, nature and consciousness, knowledge and its qualities. Use grounded interpretive scenes; do not label philosophical entities or imply one human body is the entire incorporeal Self. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: That is the Light of lights, said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the Knowable, and the goal of knowledge — established in the heart of all. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Know both Prakṛti and Puruṣa to be beginningless. And know that modifications (vikāras) and the guṇas are born from Prakṛti. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene. Phone-first composition update, owner 2026-10-19: phones are the primary reading device, tablets secondary. Keep the complete meaningful scene compact and intelligible at 320–430 logical pixels wide. Arrange the important relationships as one close, coherent central grouping; avoid essential tiny distant figures and wide edge-to-edge action. Keep generous quiet margins on all four sides, no faces, hands, feet, narrative objects or important background subjects touching the frame. The complete portrait painting will be contained inside the phone reading area, never stretched or cropped to fill it; do not depend on edge cropping. Preserve the approved watercolor style and the exact verse meaning. No labels, letters, sacred syllables, explanatory marks or typography. Portrait-format owner update 2026-10-19: create a genuinely tall 9:16 painted composition for phone reading, not a square painting pasted on blank portrait paper. The atmosphere and natural scene should continue organically through the portrait canvas. Keep all important subjects wholly visible, inside quiet margins; no frame-edge clipping. Use one coherent compact narrative group, with detail readable on a phone. This same portrait painting is reused proportionally on tablets and landscape screens; do not create a second image for tablets.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 13.18: Thus the Field, Knowledge, and the Knowable have been described in brief. My devotee, knowing this through direct realization (vijñāna), attains My very being.
